answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with time-locked fidelity bonds. Each agent locks minimum collateral in an escrow contract for a fixed epoch to hold one rate-limited identity, losing that stake if fraud proofs show cheating. Raising a costly terrace above an economic ledge instead of a shifting dune of free keys, this imposes verifiable illiquid capital and slashing risk per fake identity. However, wealthy adversaries can still fund multiple accounts when bond thresholds stay low.
